title: Spiritual ecumenism
hookLine: Vatican II calls prayer the soul of Christian unity

lines: HE ASKED THAT THEY BE ONE.
cards: On the night before he died, Jesus prayed out loud for the people who would come after his friends, people he would never meet. John's Gospel keeps the words.
He didn't ask that they be clever, or successful, or even safe. He asked that they be one. Christians have argued, split and sometimes fought ever since.
And when the Catholic Church sat down at the Second Vatican Council to ask how to mend those splits, it put something before the meetings and the documents.

teach.h: THAT THEY ALL MAY BE ONE.
teach.b: You met this prayer on day five hundred twenty-five, and the Week of Prayer for Christian Unity on day six hundred forty-seven.

In the Douay-Rheims, John chapter seventeen: "That they all may be one, as thou, Father, in me, and I in thee; that they also may be one in us; that the world may believe that thou hast sent me." Notice the last clause.
Unity isn't only about Christians getting along; it's tied to whether the world can believe at all.

Ecumenism is the work of Christians from divided churches seeking the unity Jesus prayed for. It includes theologians in dialogue and joint statements, and you'll meet some of those in the coming days.
But the council's decree on ecumenism put something first.

teach.h: PRAYER IS THE SOUL OF IT.
teach.b: It says that a change of heart and holiness of life, together with public and private prayer for the unity of Christians, should be seen as the soul of the whole ecumenical movement.
And it gives this a name: spiritual ecumenism. The soul, the decree says: not decoration on top of the real work, but what makes the work alive.

The same decree says Catholics may, in certain circumstances, join in prayer with other Christians for unity. That's the week of prayer, when churches that can't yet share one altar still share one prayer.
In the council's picture, changed hearts are the soul of the work, and the documents serve them.
A dialogue between people who have prayed together starts from a different place than a negotiation between strangers.

how: Catholics pray for Christian unity at Mass and in private, and join other Christians in shared services of prayer, especially during the week of prayer for Christian unity.

games.q: you're at the council, asked how divided Christians can come back together. what goes first?
o: change of heart and prayer for unity.
a vote on who was right.
games.why: the decree on ecumenism calls change of heart, holiness and prayer the soul of the ecumenical movement, and names it spiritual ecumenism.

practice: Bring to mind one Christian you know from a different church, a Baptist neighbor, an Orthodox coworker, a cousin whose church has a band, and hold their face for a moment.
If you pray, pray for them and for unity in the words of John seventeen: that they all may be one. If you don't pray, hold them in mind with goodwill.

wordCard.voice: Spiritual ecumenism. Change of heart, holiness of life and prayer for unity, which the council called the soul of the ecumenical movement. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: prayer first. Hearts first, and then the documents. Until tomorrow.
